long_biography.plain_text:
At eighteen, a job in his uncle’s Naples roastery gave Massimo Renda practical command of production and sales. After an idea for automatic distribution was declined, he struck out in the early 1990s, building Renda Distributori client by client. He then created L’Aromatika in 1997, taking roasting, packaging and commercial execution under his own control.

The Caffè Borbone name followed as pods and capsules began changing how Italians drank espresso. Renda combined efficient high-volume production with specialist retail, online sales, supermarket expansion and conspicuous popular advertising. Italmobiliare acquired a majority stake in 2018, while he retained a minority interest and remained executive chairman. The business became a nationally prominent single-serve coffee producer, and his industrial record brought appointment as a Cavaliere del Lavoro.
